n: God addresses Israel, descended from Judah, who use His name in oaths and worship but without sincerity. Nephi quotes this chapter as 1 Nephi 20 and adds the phrase “or out of the waters of baptism,” linking covenant birth to baptism.

f.w: come forth out of the waters of Judah
f.g: Descended from Judah, as from a spring; the Book of Mormon adds “or out of the waters of baptism.”

f.w: but not in truth, nor in righteousness

n: They claim the holy city as home and say they lean on God, yet their hearts aren’t in it. Nephi’s version begins, “Nevertheless, they call themselves of the holy city,” but adds that they do not stay themselves on God.

f.w: stay themselves upon
they call themselves of the holy city

n: God announced past events long before they happened, then suddenly brought them to pass.

f.w: I have declared the former things from the beginning

n: Why announce things ahead of time? Because God knew Israel was stubborn—a neck like iron that wouldn’t bow, a forehead hard as bronze.

f.w: thy neck is an iron sinew
f.g: An unbending neck—stubbornness, like an ox refusing the yoke.

f.w: thy brow brass

n: He told them beforehand so they couldn’t credit their idols when it happened.
You’ve heard and seen it—won’t you admit it? Now God reveals new, hidden things they never knew before.

f.w: new things

n: These new things are being created now, not long ago, so Israel can’t say, “I already knew that.”
Israel never really listened—their ears were closed. God knew they would be treacherous, rebels from birth. Even so, His plan included them.

f.w: a transgressor from the womb

n: For the sake of His name and praise, God holds back His anger so as not to wipe Israel out. Mercy flows from His character.

f.w: For my name's sake

n: God has refined Israel—not like silver in a smelter, but through the furnace of suffering. Hard trials can purify and prepare a chosen people.

f.w: the furnace of affliction
I have chosen thee
f.g: Some manuscripts read “I have tested you.”

n: God acts for His own sake so His name won’t be dishonored, and He won’t give His glory to anyone else. 1 Nephi 20:11 reads, “for I will not suffer my name to be polluted.”

f.w: how should my name be polluted?
I will not give my glory unto another

n: Listen, My called ones: I am He, the First and the Last. These titles belong to Jehovah, whom Latter-day Saints know as Jesus Christ.

f.w: I am the first, I also am the last

n: His hand laid earth’s foundations and spread the heavens; when He calls, they all stand at attention.

f.w: my right hand hath spanned the heavens

n: Which idol foretold this? The Lord loves the one He has chosen (Cyrus), who will carry out His will against Babylon. Nephi’s version adds that the Lord “will fulfil his word which he hath declared by them.”

f.w: The LORD hath loved him

n: God Himself has spoken and called this deliverer; He will make his mission succeed.

Come close and listen: God has always spoken openly. Then a voice says, “Now the Lord God and His Spirit have sent me.” Many Christians and Latter-day Saints hear the Messiah speaking here, with the Father and the Spirit also present.

f.w: I have not spoken in secret
the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me

n: The Redeemer teaches Israel what is truly good for them and leads them in the path they should take.

f.w: which teacheth thee to profit
f.g: Teaches you what is for your benefit.

f.w: leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go

n: A heartfelt sigh from God: if only you had obeyed! Your peace would have flowed like a river and your righteousness rolled in like ocean waves. Nephi quoted this, and Lehi’s family heard it again in the wilderness.

f.w: then had thy peace been as a river

n: Their descendants would have been countless as sand—the promise made to Abraham—and their name never cut off.

f.w: Thy seed also had been as the sand

n: Get out of Babylon! Flee the Chaldeans and shout to the ends of the earth that the Lord has redeemed Jacob. Latter-day scripture repeats this call to leave spiritual Babylon—worldliness.

f.w: Go ye forth of Babylon

n: Just as God gave Israel water from the rock in the Sinai desert, He will care for them on the journey home.

f.w: he caused the waters to flow out of the rock

n: A sobering close: there is no peace for the wicked. Nephi’s version begins, “And notwithstanding he hath done all this, and greater also,” stressing that even great blessings can’t give peace to those who refuse God.

f.w: There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked
